analysis.investment_thesis: Gravita is a genuine circular-economy play benefiting from India's EPR mandates and battery recycling boom, with an exceptional 58.4% net profit CAGR over 9 years. However, at ₹11,951 Cr market cap and P/E of 31.7x, it has already been discovered — this is not the Kedia entry point; this is where Kedia books profits.
key_strengths: Structural tailwind is real — Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 (EPR mandates) force compliance recycling, Gravita is the incumbent beneficiary
Exceptional profit compounding: net profit grew from ₹5 Cr (2016) to ₹313 Cr (2025), 58.4% CAGR, with margins visibly expanding over 5 years
Conservative balance sheet — D/E at 0.20 and promoter at 55.88% with steady holding; OCF positive all 5 years
key_risks: Market cap of ₹11,951 Cr is 6–12x outside Kedia's sweet spot; information asymmetry is gone — FII owns 15.75%
Other Income of ₹111 Cr in FY25 (vs ₹1–6 Cr pre-FY23) inflates reported PAT of ₹313 Cr; strip it out and core earnings power is ~₹235 Cr, pushing adjusted P/E above 50x
Massive ₹864 Cr investing outflow + ₹640 Cr financing inflow in FY25 signals large equity raise (equity jumped ₹837→₹2,260 Cr) — aggressive dilution at premium valuations
red_flags: P/E 31.7x — nearly double Kedia's 8–15x ceiling even for quality small-caps
Equity base nearly tripled in FY25 (₹837 Cr → ₹2,260 Cr) via QIP — dilutes per-share earnings trajectory
Other income suspiciously high (₹88/76/111 Cr last 3 years vs near-zero prior) — quality of reported ₹313 Cr PAT is questionable
FCF volatile and negative in FY22 and FY24 (-₹61 Cr, -₹56 Cr) — capital-intensive business erodes free cash quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Gravita is a fundamentally sound business operating in a secular trend — secondary lead, aluminium and plastic recycling driven by India's EPR compliance framework. Revenue has compounded at 27.6% for 9 years (₹430 Cr → ₹3,869 Cr) and operating profit at 38.1%, demonstrating operating leverage. The EPR regulations mandating battery collection/recycling are a legitimate transformation catalyst, and Gravita's established capacity and compliance infrastructure gives it a genuine moat in a fragmented sector. The 0.20 D/E and 21.5% ROCE confirm capital efficiency. This is a quality business — but quality at the right price is the Kedia mantra.

The problem is simple: at ₹11,951 Cr this is a mid-cap the market has already re-rated aggressively. Kedia's magic happens at ₹100–1,000 Cr, not ₹12,000 Cr. The FY25 financials contain two alarm bells — "Other Income" of ₹111 Cr (EPR certificates? forex? unclear) that props up PAT, and a massive equity raise that nearly tripled the equity base, implying the promoters themselves chose to sell at these levels. FII ownership at 15.75% confirms institutional discovery is complete. The entry window for a Kedia-style multibagger was five years ago around ₹500–800 Cr market cap. Today's buyer is paying growth stock valuations (P/E 31.7x, EV/EBITDA 24.5x) for a commodity-adjacent recycler with moderate 12% operating margins.
